The following table lists many specialized [[symbol]]s commonly used in modern [[mathematics]], ordered by their introduction date.

| [[Christoff Rudolff]]

| 1556
| [[Nicolo Tartaglia]]

| [[equals sign]]

| [[Robert Recorde]]
|-

| [[decimal separator]]

| [[Christopher Clavius]]

| [[multiplication sign]]

| [[William Oughtred]]
|-

| [[plus–minus sign]]
| 1628
| [[William Oughtred]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">∷</div>
| [[proportion sign]]
| 1628
| [[William Oughtred]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;"><sup>''n''</sup>√</div>
| radical symbol (for [[nth root|''n''th root]])
| 1629
| [[Albert Girard]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;"><<br />></div>
| [[strict inequality]] signs (''less-than sign'' and ''greater-than sign'')
| 1631
| [[Thomas Harriot]]
|-
| rowspan=2 bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">''x<sup>y</sup>''</div>
| rowspan=2| [[superscript]] notation (for [[exponentiation]])
| 1636
| [[James Hume (mathematician)|James Hume]]
| Using [[Roman numerals]] as superscripts.
|-
| 1637<ref name="boyer1991">{{Citation| first=Carl B.| last=Boyer| author-link=Carl Benjamin Boyer| title=A History of Mathematics| edition=Second| publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc.| year=1991| isbn=978-0-471-54397-8| url=https://archive.org/details/historyofmathema00boye}}</ref>
| [[René Descartes]]
| In ''[[La Géométrie]]''. In the modern form.
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center font-size=200%| <div style="font-size:200%;">''x''</div> 
| Use of [[History of algebra#The symbol x|the letter ''x'']] for an [[independent variable]] or unknown value.
| 1637<ref name="boyer1991" />
| [[René Descartes]]
| In ''[[La Géométrie]]''.
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">√ ̅ </div>
| radical symbol (for [[square root]])
| 1637<ref name="boyer1991" />
| [[René Descartes]]
| In ''[[La Géométrie]]''. With the [[vinculum (symbol)|vinculum]] above the [[radicand]].
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">%</div>
| [[percent sign]]
| {{circa|1650|sortable=yes}}
| unknown
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">∞</div>
| [[infinity]] sign
| 1655
| [[John Wallis]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">÷</div>
| [[division sign]]
| 1659
| [[Johann Rahn]] or [[John Pell (mathematician)|John Pell]]
| Originated as a repurposed [[obelus]] variant.
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">∴</div>
| [[therefore sign]]
| 1659
| [[Johann Rahn]] or [[John Pell (mathematician)|John Pell]]
|-
| rowspan=2 bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">≤<br />≥</div>
| rowspan=2| [[inequality (mathematics)|unstrict inequality signs]] (''less-than or equals to sign'' and ''greater-than or equals to sign'')
| 1670
| [[John Wallis]]
| With the horizontal bar above the inequality sign.
|-
| 1734
| [[Pierre Bouguer]]
| With double horizontal bar below the inequality sign.
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">d</div>
| [[differential (calculus)|differential]] sign
| 1675
| [[Gottfried Leibniz]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">∫</div>
| [[integral sign]]
| 1675
| [[Gottfried Leibniz]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">:</div>
| [[colon (punctuation)|colon]] (for [[division (mathematics)|division]])
| 1684
| [[Gottfried Leibniz]]
| Derives from the use of the colon to denote fractions, dating back to 1633.
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">·</div>
| [[middle dot]] (for [[multiplication]])
| 1698
| [[Gottfried Leibniz]]
| Perhaps derives from a much earlier use of the middle dot to separate juxtaposed numbers.
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">π</div>
| [[pi]] (ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter)
| 1706
| [[William Jones (mathematician)|William Jones]]
| Believed to have been used because ''p'' (π) is the first letter in ''perimetron'' (perimeter).
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center|<div style="font-size:200%;">⁄</div>
| [[slash (punctuation)|division slash]] (a.k.a. ''solidus'')
| 1718
| [[Thomas Twining (merchant)|Thomas Twining]]
| Derives from the horizontal [[fraction bar]].
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">''e''</div>
| [[e (mathematical constant)|''e'']] (the base of the [[natural logarithm]])
| 1727–1728
| [[Leonhard Euler]]
| Unpublished. First published appearance was in Euler's ''[[Mechanica]]'' (1736).
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">≠</div>
| [[inequality (mathematics)|inequality]] sign (''not equal to'')
| unknown
| [[Leonhard Euler]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">''x''{{prime}}</div>
| [[prime symbol]] (for [[derivative]])
| 1748
| [[Leonhard Euler]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">Σ</div>
| [[summation]] symbol
| 1755
| [[Leonhard Euler]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">∝</div>
| [[proportionality (mathematics)|proportionality]] sign
| 1768
| [[William Emerson (mathematician)|William Emerson]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">∂</div>
| [[partial differential]] sign
| 1770
| [[Marquis de Condorcet]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">''i''</div>
| [[imaginary number]]
| 1777
| [[Leonhard Euler]]
| Used in a memoir. First publisher by Euler in 1794 in his ''Institutionum calculi integralis''.
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">≡</div>
| [[Identity (mathematics)|identity]] sign (for [[congruence relation]])
| 1801
| [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]]
| First appearance in print, used previously in personal writings of Gauss.
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">[''x'']</div>
| ''integral part'' (a.k.a. [[floor and ceiling functions|floor]])
| 1808
| [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">!</div>
| [[factorial]]
| 1808
| [[Christian Kramp]]
|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">Π</div>
| [[multiplication|product]] symbol
| 1812
| [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]]
|-
| rowspan=2 bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">⊂<br />⊃</div>
| rowspan=2| [[set inclusion]] signs (''subset of'', ''superset of'')
| 1817
| [[Joseph Gergonne]]
|-
| 1890
| [[Ernst Schröder (mathematician)|Ernst Schröder]]
|-
| rowspan=2 bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">|...|</div>
| [[absolute value]] notation
| 1841
| [[Karl Weierstrass]]
|-
| [[determinant]] of a matrix
| 1841

| [[Arthur Cayley]]

| [[Giuseppe Peano]]

| [[logical disjunction]] (a.k.a. ''OR'')
| 1906
| [[Bertrand Russell]]
|-
| rowspan=2 bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;">(...)<br />[...]</div>
| rowspan=2| [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] notation
| rowspan=2| 1909<ref name="matrix" />
| [[Maxime Bôcher]]
|-
| [[Gerhard Kowalewski]]

| [[line integral|contour integral]] sign

| [[Edmund Landau]]

|-
| bgcolor=#d0f0d0 align=center| <div style="font-size:200%;"  class="Unicode"><math>\mathbb{C}</math></div>
| [[Blackboard bold]] capital C (for [[complex number]]s set)
| 1939
| [[Nathan Jacobson]]
|-

| [[Paul Halmos]]

| [[Kenneth E. Iverson]]
